leads:
Items 3-6 are observations from the bytes that were not run on hardware.

1. Older-build remnants exist in prom_b. Three are proven, each by its own script under notes/promb-2026-09-25/:
   - 0xF0ED50-0xF0EFFF is live minus 0x23001 (`stale_dl_tables_f0ed50.py`).
   - 0xF17A5F-0xF17BFF is live minus 0x1A401 (`stale_value_glyphs_f17a5f.py`).
   - 0xF6F000-0xF6F3FF is live minus 0xBA00 (`old_module_copy_f6f000.py`).

   Each runs from the end of this build's code to a 1 KB or 4 KB boundary and is named by nothing. `relocated_copy_scan.py --boundaries` lists further candidates to check. Most candidates will be legitimate repeats, but any unreferenced run ending on a 1 KB boundary deserves a look. prom_a may hold the same kind of remnant. This may matter for MAME: code that looks unreached may be stale, not a missed call path.

2. The 0xF3F400 records are the factory-default image of the ParamNumber_RecordPtrs parameter records.
   - They give the parts' default MIDI channels (part k gets channel k; part 9, channel 10, differs).
   - They give the DSP effect defaults (algorithms 1, 35, 20).
   - A prom_a lane could name the loaders: sub_FAAE2A / sub_FAAF91 / sub_FAA967 look like reset-to-defaults routines. It could also give meanings to the other 11 ids.

3. `SmfSysEx_WriteAddr11` has `cp XDE,0xffffffff` before `ld XDE,(XDE)`, so it compares the pointer, not the entry. As written, SysEx address 11:lo with an empty (0xFFFFFFFF) entry writes through to 0xFFFFFF. This is worth a MAME trace.

4. DLRecordPtrs_F03173's readers index entries 19-20, past the table and into DL_F031BF (A = 18/19 in the pairing site, A = 7 in the one-record site).

5. TouchCurve_BoxOrigins3[0] says x = 0xA8, but its list's box starts at 0xE0.

6. The Japanese text finding (commit cf53cdf6), the FINDINGS content the harness blocked. DL_F2E91A (0xF2E91A-0xF2E9E2, 28 A-records) is the firmware's only Japanese text: two 14-record messages split at 0xF2E97A.
   - Message 1: 「コードトラックがすでにあります。2つのトラックをコードトラックに指定できません。」 ("A chord track already exists; two tracks cannot be assigned as chord tracks.")
   - Message 2: the same with コントロールトラック (control track).
   - Record ops are 0x19/0x1D/0x1A (kana/kanji faces) and 0x07 (Latin 8x16).
   - Small katakana 0x46 = ッ and 0x3E = ァ, verified by glyph.
   - 0xF2E91A appears 8 times in prom_a's PtrTable_F99121, always as the END of DL_Error (0xF2E910-0xF2E91A). 0xF2E97A is spelled nowhere, so neither Japanese list is proven reachable.
   - 151 op-0x1C records use service 0x1C (Font_Svc1C).
   - Checked by `japanese_messages_probe.py`.
